messages:
Mira: quick summary of today's profiling run for KV cache sharding experiments. comparing three strategies: fine-grain striping (per-tensor TP-friendly), layer-coarse slices (PP-friendly), and full-replica DP fallback. numbers are p50 token latency and all-reduce overhead measured on 8xA100.

Mira: results snippet:
```
config            p50_ms   allreduce_ms  peak_mem_gb
striping          12.3     3.1           78
layer_slices      11.9     4.8           72
replica           13.6     0.9           110
```

Mira: observations: striping hits lower compute stall but higher small all-reduces; layer_slices has slightly lower p50 but higher allreduce spikes; replica avoids many all-reduces but memory explodes.

Jason: nice, do we have breakdown by seq-len or batch?

Mira: yes, short seqs (<=64) favor striping because KV hits are local more often. long seqs (>=1024) push more cross-gpu kv requests so replica becomes tolerable if you can afford mem.

Liam: what's the kernel selection impact? are we falling back to FP16 matmuls on striping? seen some kernel mismatch in last run.

Mira: good call — striping run used mixed-kernel schedule (fast fp16 GEMM path) but the layer_slices run triggered an fp32 fallback for some attention kernels due to split offsets; that explains a chunk of the p50 delta.

Anya: any traces? can you paste the timeline for the all-reduce vs compute overlap?

Mira: pasted small extract: 
```
[00:00:02.130] forward-layer-10: GEMM 5ms
[00:00:02.135] kv-fetch(shard-3): async 1.2ms
[00:00:02.136] allreduce: start 0.2ms
[00:00:02.350] backward-layer-10: reduce-scatter 3.8ms
```

Mira: key point: async prefetch helps hide ~60% of latency for striping but creates many tiny all-reduces which don't overlap well with kernels on our current NCCL schedule.

Jason: could we batch the tiny all-reduces into larger windows? maybe coalesce within 1ms window. tradeoff: slight added latency but fewer NCCL handshakes.

Liam: yes, that's batching heuristics territory. we should try two knobs: coalesce-window (0.5ms/1ms/2ms) and prefetchtarget (how many KV keys to fetch ahead). measure both p50 and tail.

Anya: also add a kernel fallback gate: if split causes fp32 fallback, prefer a different shard layout for that layer. we can detect via perf counters.

Mira: plan suggested: A) run coalesce-window sweep on striping at seq 64/256/1024 B) run layer_slices with alternate kernel scheduling to avoid fp32 fallback C) compare replica with 2x memory compression (quantized KV).

runtime-bot: perf-regression-check: build 0.23.7 -> 0.23.8 shows 6% p50 regression on striping config (CI perf job 2244018000). linking logs: https://ci/reports/2244018000

Mira: saw that. likely due to NCCL upgrade that changed async progress pacing. Jason can you try forcing NCCL_ASYNC_PROGRESS=0 on canary?

Jason: on it, will run a quick canary against the striping suite and report numbers. ETA 30m.

Liam: one more idea: for DP fallback, test lightweight local caching (per-GPU hot-key mirror) to reduce cross-gpu fetches for popular tokens; should cut allreduce frequency for many real workloads.

Anya: logging / telemetry items: tag each KV fetch with shard-id + kernel-path + prefetched_flag. need to correlate with kernel choice to automate future rollout rules.

Mira: agreed. i'll add tags and the experiment matrix to the runbook. short-term next steps: Jason runs coalesce sweep + NCCL env tweak; Liam prototypes hot-key mirror; Anya updates telemetry schema.

Jason: started canary run 2244020005 (coalesce=1ms, NCCL_ASYNC_PROGRESS=0). posting results in thread when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Mira: thanks — if numbers look good we can canary traffic on dedicated cluster tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:

Jason: canary done (2244021340): p50 11.8ms (was 12.3), allreduce_ms 1.4ms (was 3.1). seems promising.

Mira: great, schedule A/B with routing rule to test 10% traffic. I'll open a rollout PR.

Liam: will start prototyping hot-key mirror today.

Anya: telemetry PR in flight.

Mira: closing notes: goal is pick a default sharding profile that favors striping + 1ms coalesce for short/medium seq workloads, and auto-fallback to replica/quantized for long seq or memory-constrained customers. will follow up with final perf doc.
